title: Hotfix: avoid cooldown/clamp interaction that can stall scale-down
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Context
We hit an edge case after enabling bounded autoscaling for a small set of Dedicated pools: scale-down could effectively “stall” for long periods when cooldown was enabled and the controller was repeatedly clamping the computed desired replicas. Operators observed pools staying above the expected steady-state (burning spend) even though demand dropped and reactive signals suggested scale-down.

Incident reference
- Slack: sources/slack/incidents/1707075532 (bounded max + insufficient pre-scale; follow-on investigation found scale-down stall)
- Support: SUP-4965 ("Dedicated pool stuck at min after rollout"; triage pointed to cooldown/clamp interaction)

Root cause
The autoscaler updates its cooldown bookkeeping any time it produces a “scale event”. In the current flow, we compute desired_replicas from signals, apply cooldown logic, then clamp to bounds (min/max). When the unclamped desired fluctuates below min (or above max), we would repeatedly “decide” a scale step (pre-clamp) even though the applied replicas after clamping did not change. That incorrectly refreshed last_scale_{up,down}_at and kept the controller in cooldown, preventing legitimate scale-down from being applied once the computed desired moved back within bounds.

Fix
- Only record a scale event / update cooldown timestamps when the *applied* replicas change (post-clamp actuation), not when the *pre-clamp* desired changes.
- Treat clamp-only outcomes as a separate decision type (for auditability) that does not affect cooldown.
- Add targeted unit/integration tests to cover: (1) oscillating desired below min with cooldown enabled does not starve future scale-down, (2) clamp-to-min does not reset scale-down cooldown, (3) clamp reasons are still emitted.

Notes
This is intentionally minimal and safe to backport if needed. No changes to bounds semantics; only the ordering/bookkeeping around cooldown state.

Rollout
- Hotfix is gated behind the existing bounded-autoscaling allowlist. Once merged, SRE will monitor clamp_reason + scale_apply_latency dashboards for the design partners for 24h before expanding.

Checklist
- [x] Added regression tests
- [x] Verified structured decision logs include clamp-only decisions
- [x] Confirmed no metrics cardinality increase (reused existing clamp_reason label)
- [x] Added brief runbook note for interpreting the new decision type
commits: autoscaler: only advance cooldown on applied actuation
autoscaler: classify clamp-only decisions (no cooldown impact)
tests: regression coverage for cooldown+clamp stall
docs: note clamp-only decisions in decision log schema
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz: Can you clarify what we’ll see in logs after this change? I want to make sure operators can still tell we’re clamping even if it doesn’t count as a scale event.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep. Decision logs will still emit clamp_reason + desired_replicas_raw vs desired_replicas_applied. I added `decision_type=clamp_only` when raw!=applied and applied==current, so it’s visible but won’t touch cooldown timestamps.
Jordan Lee: Any chance this changes semantics around min during drains/maintenance? We were careful in ADR-0142 about not treating min as absolute during drain scenarios.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): No change to min semantics. This only affects cooldown bookkeeping. If drain/maintenance forces an override, that path still sets `override_reason` and will update cooldown only when we actually change applied replicas.
Allison Grant: Please confirm metrics labels didn’t get new high-cardinality dimensions. Also, do we page on clamp_only spikes?

Keiko Yamamoto (author): No new labels. We reuse existing `clamp_reason` and add `decision_type` only in structured logs (not metrics). No paging change in this PR. Clamp_only spikes are expected under low demand when min is > 0; dashboards already have clamp panels.

Sean Gallagher: I’d like a test that matches the SUP-4965 symptom: we oscillate under min for N loops with cooldown enabled, then demand settles within bounds; we should scale down within one cooldown interval and not keep extending it.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added `TestCooldownNotExtendedByClampOnly` and an integration-style loop in `bounded_autoscaling_test` that reproduces the behavior. Links SUP-4965 in test comment for traceability.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approving. Please make sure this is included in the next fleet hotfix bundle notes.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added release note below; Connor will pick it up in the bundle.
release_notes: - Dedicated autoscaler: fixed an issue where cooldown bookkeeping could be incorrectly refreshed by clamp-only decisions, potentially delaying scale-down within customer bounds.
